title: Team Talk: Handling Requests at Work · 独立口语迁移
instructions: 先完成示范段的跟读诊断，再用不同人物、信息或立场录制自己的完整回答。示范与自由回答分别取证，服务未提供完整听音评阅时保持待评。
reference: At a small company, four team members meet on Monday morning. They talk about work requests. A request is a job someone asks you to do. The team has many requests this week. They must decide who does what. “I have to finish the sales report today,” says Mia. “It is for the manager. I cannot help with other work this morning.” Tom says, “I must call three customers. They have questions about our new product. I can do that after lunch.” “Last week, we had a big problem,” says Leo. “We said ‘yes’ to every request. Then we were very busy. We did not finish our own work. We have to say ‘no’ sometimes. We must ask: Is this request important? Is it for today?” “I can make a simple plan,” says Mia. “We can write all requests on the board. Then we can see the busy times. We have to check the plan every morning.
prompt:
Part 1
Do you have to work or study on weekends?
What can you do well at work or at school?
Did you have a busy day yesterday?
Do you make a plan every morning?

Part 2
Describe a time when you had to say ‘no’ to a request. You should say: what the request was; who asked you; why you said ‘no’; and how you felt after that.

Part 3
Why do some people say ‘yes’ to every request?
Is it important to have a plan for the week? Why?
What can a team do when it has too much work?
How did people manage time before computers?
